        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>

                </div>
            </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

ABOUT ARCHIMED

With offices in Europe, the US and Asia, ARCHIMED is a leading investment firm focused exclusively on healthcare. Our mix of operational, medical, scientific and financial expertise positions us as both a strategic and financial partner to healthcare businesses. Priority areas include Biopharma Products, Consumer Health, Healthcare IT, In Vitro Diagnostics, Life Science Tools and Biologic Services, MedTech and Pharma Services. ARCHIMED helps partners internationalize, acquire, innovate and expand their products and services.

ARCHIMED manages $11 billion across its funds, including the largest healthcare-only private equity fund raised by a European-based GP. MED I, MED II and MED Platform I are all top-decile performers for their vintage according to Preqin data. Since inception, ARCHIMED has been a committed impact investor, both directly and through its EURÊKA Foundation.

THE TEAM

  • An global team with complementary backgrounds across investment, medical, scientific, strategic and operational disciplines.
  • Alumni of INSEAD, Wharton, Berkeley, Georgetown, Bocconi, HEC Paris, École des Ponts ParisTech, ESSEC, Imperial College and Dartmouth, among others.
  • Professional backgrounds spanning Private Equity (3i, Siparex, USS Ltd, Barings, Capiton, Partners Group, KKR), Consulting (A.T. Kearney, Bain, McKinsey), M&A (Lazard, EY, KPMG, PwC, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies) and Industry (Biotronik, Cerba, Stryker, Phillips, Pfizer, Baxter, LivaNova, J&J, Galderma, Sanofi).

THE DIAGNOSTICS TEAM

The Director will serve as a senior investment professional with direct responsibility for sourcing, evaluating and executing investments across the Diagnostics portfolio. The Director will lead deal activity across an assigned geography, technology platform or investment theme, and will carry accountability for investment outcomes, value creation and portfolio company support.

This is a senior operating role combining strategic direction setting with hands-on deal execution, positioning the Director as a trusted senior advisor to Partners and portfolio management teams.

  • Investment Sourcing & Strategy
    • Drive sourcing and pipeline development across assigned Diagnostics sectors or geographies, identifying and cultivating relationships with sellers, intermediaries and LP co-investors.
    • Lead the formation and evolution of investment theses within assigned focus areas, including category mapping, competitive positioning and market trend analysis.
    • Serve as primary investment decision maker and deal sponsor, with direct accountability for investment committee presentations and recommendation.
    • Lead the negotiation of transaction terms, pricing and deal structure in partnership with Partners and external advisors.
  • Due Diligence & Execution
    • Oversee comprehensive commercial, financial and operational due diligence, working with external advisors to validate assumptions and identify key risks and levers.
    • Lead the development of post-acquisition value creation roadmaps, including 100-day plans and multi-year operating strategies.
    • Manage the investment committee approval process and coordinate all transaction closing mechanics with legal and finance teams.
  • Portfolio Leadership & Value Creation
    • Serve as the primary investment relationship owner for assigned portfolio companies, working directly with management teams on strategy, M&A, capital deployment and operational priorities.
    • Lead add-on acquisition identification, evaluation and execution, including syndication with co-investors.
    • Drive performance monitoring and problem-solving, escalating key decisions to Partners and intervention areas to senior management.
    • Sponsor and mentor portfolio company boards, ensuring robust governance and strategic clarity.
  • Team & Platform Development
    • Mentor and develop Senior Analysts and Associate-level team members, contributing to talent development and succession planning within the Diagnostics function.
    • Contribute to ARCHIMED's Diagnostics thought leadership and external positioning through conference participation, investor communication and industry engagement.
    • Identify and build capabilities across the Diagnostics platform to support scaling and evolution of the investment program.

Requirements

  • 8 to 12 years of investment or operating experience, with a strong track record in private equity investing, transaction execution or operational leadership within diagnostics sector.
  • Demonstrated success originating, evaluating and closing significant investments (€50 million+ enterprise value preferred), with evidence of value creation across the portfolio.
  • Deep expertise in the Diagnostics landscape, including brand strategy, omnichannel distribution, and regulatory dynamics .
  • Exceptional executive presence and communication skills. Able to command credibility with sophisticated management teams, institutional LPs and external partners.
  • Strong financial acumen and fluency with investment modeling, valuation and deal structuring. Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills required.
  • Proven operational judgment and the ability to translate market insights into concrete investment theses and deal opportunities.
  • Track record of building and leading high-performing teams. Comfort with mentoring junior professionals and shaping investment culture.
  • Strategic, entrepreneurial and partnership-minded. Takes ownership of outcomes, moves with pace and brings a builder's orientation to platform development.
  • Advanced degree preferred. MBA or equivalent experience strongly valued.
  • Embodies and reinforces ARCHIMED's cultural values of inclusion, meritocracy, partnership, accountability, client focus and trust.

Bumble Inc. is looking for an Operations Specialist, AI Enablement to join our CX & Trust team. Trust, care, and high-quality experiences are central to Bumble’s mission to create a world where all relationships are healthy and equitable, and in this role you’ll help bring that mission to life by improving how our AI-powered customer experience and moderation systems support our community.

Through quality reviews, accurate case labelling, golden-set maintenance, and thoughtful analysis, you’ll help ensure AI-supported decisions are consistent, precise, and grounded in the nuance required to serve our members responsibly.   • Use QA platforms and AI-supported tools, including systems such as Cinder, Zendesk QA, and Bumble’s internal assessment tooling, to monitor quality and understand AI behaviour, reviewing outputs critically for accuracy, bias, privacy, and fairness and applying human judgment before acting on results.

The Role

Intellect delivers a clinically governed mental health programme to enterprise clients in the mining and resources sector, supporting remote and expatriate workforces. This is not a standard EAP. Cases begin with acute risk assessment on remote sites and run through structured treatment, fitness-for-work assessment and return-to-work clearance, in direct coordination with the client's chaplaincy, medical and people teams.

This role covers the client's United Kingdom operations and a West African project site where the working language is French. It is a combined clinical delivery and case management role: the postholder conducts the assessments, delivers the therapy, writes the reports and owns the case, rather than coordinating a provider network. That design reflects the absence of an established provider network in the West African market at launch, and gives the client a single clinician who knows each case end to end.

Full professional fluency in French and English is a non-negotiable requirement. Welfare calls, clinical assessment, case documentation and client communication in the West African market are conducted in French.

Responsibilities

Clinical assessment and delivery

  • Conduct acute risk and welfare assessments for employees referred through the client's escalation pathway, in French or English as required.
  • Deliver individual counselling and psychotherapy across the supported caseload, virtually.
  • Conduct fitness-for-work assessments and produce the associated clinical documentation.
  • Write risk assessments, session documentation, return-to-work memoranda and fitness-for-work reports to a standard that stands up to client and regulatory scrutiny, in the language the case requires.
  • Delivery is capped so that case management availability is protected. Session load is agreed with the Head of Clinical Operations and reviewed as volume changes.

Case management and coordination

  • Own each case end to end, from referral through assessment, treatment, fitness-for-work and reintegration to closure.
  • Align the initial support plan with the client's on-site teams, including session volume and cadence, and manage adjustments where clinically indicated.
  • Coordinate with internal helpline, care excellence and network partnership teams on anything that cannot be delivered directly.
  • Review the open case list for stalled items and follow up to keep cases moving.

Clinical risk oversight and governance

  • Confirm risk tiering against the client's framework and set review cadence and monitoring requirements.
  • Make the clinical decisions the pathway requires, including disputed risk ratings and medical evaluation pathways where an employee declines therapy.
  • Escalate to the Head of Clinical Operations where a case exceeds the scope of remote delivery or requires in-person intervention.
  • Work within the differing regulatory, medical and emergency-escalation environments of each market, and flag where local pathways do not support the agreed protocol.

Clinical protocols and client enablement

  • Co-develop and maintain the clinical protocols, risk frameworks and SOPs the client's on-site teams operate to, including French-language versions.
  • Design and deliver clinical training and framework guidance to client-side staff who are not clinicians, in French and English.
  • Build out the in-market provider network alongside Network Partnerships, so that in-person and overflow capacity exists as the programme scales.

Client relationship, insights and reporting

  • Act as the named clinical contact for the client's chaplaincy, medical and health and safety leads in both markets, responding within the core window to queries that are frequently unscheduled and time-critical.
  • Produce the case tracker and monthly clinical reporting, moving beyond utilisation to presenting issues, risk patterns, outcomes and service-level themes.
  • Present clinical insight at client review meetings and translate it into recommendations the client's health and safety and people teams can act on.

Requirements

  • Full professional fluency in French and English, to the standard required for clinical assessment, therapy delivery and client-facing documentation in both languages.
  • Registered clinical psychologist or qualified counsellor, with current registration in your jurisdiction and the right to practise remotely.
  • Master's degree in clinical psychology, counselling or a related field.

    TopChrono, leader historique de la livraison express et du dernier kilomètre, entre dans une nouvelle ère ! Face aux mutations du secteur (explosion du e-commerce, ubérisation, nouvelles technologies), nous avons entrepris un vaste chantier de transformation, adoptant une dynamique startup pour réinventer nos solutions, activités et stratégies.

    Vous souhaitez intégrer une entreprise en pleine évolution et contribuer activement à son succès ? Ce poste est pour vous !

     

    Ce que nous vous offrons

    • Un environnement stimulant : une dynamique startup au sein d’un groupe établi (CA de 70M€, 500 collaborateurs).

    • Des opportunités d’évolution et de formation : développez vos compétences et faites avancer votre carrière.

    • Avantages sociaux : télétravail hybride, tickets restaurant, mutuelle performante, primes d’intéressement.

    • Une équipe conviviale et innovante, engagée à relever les défis d’un secteur en mutation.

    Votre rôle : fidéliser, engager et maximiser l’impact !

     

    Rattaché(e) au Rattaché(e) au Directeur des Opérations, vos principales missions sont les suivantes :

    Rattachement hiérarchique

    • Encadre un à deux collaborateur(s) en charge du suivi quotidien de la métrologie sur l'ensemble des agences au

    niveau national.

     

    Mission principale

    Le Responsable Métrologie garantit la conformité métrologique des équipements utilisés pour le transport des échantillons biologiques. Il est responsable de l'étude, du choix, de l'installation et du suivi des matériels permettant d'assurer le maintien de la chaîne de température réglementaire dans les véhicules frigorifiques. Il travaille en étroite collaboration avec le Responsable Parc Automobile, les Responsables Exploitation et les fournisseurs afin d'assurer la fiabilité des équipements et la qualité du transport.

     

    PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES

    Métrologie et maîtrise de la température

    • Définir et mettre en œuvre la politique métrologique de l'entreprise.

    • Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires relatives au transport des échantillons biologiques.

    • Assurer le suivi des équipements de mesure de température (capteurs, enregistreurs, sondes, etc.).

    • Organiser les opérations de vérification, d'étalonnage et de qualification des équipements.

    • Analyser les dérives et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

    • Connaître et faire appliquer les référentiels applicables : ADR (matières biologiques catégorie B – UN3373), norme NF EN 12830 (enregistreurs de température) et NF X15-140 (étalonnage) / accréditation COFRAC.

     

    Étude et déploiement des matériels

    • Étudier les solutions techniques adaptées aux besoins de l'entreprise.

    • Définir les spécifications techniques des équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

    • Piloter l'installation des équipements frigorifiques et des systèmes de surveillance embarqués.

    • Participer à la validation des nouveaux véhicules et matériels.

    • Assurer la maîtrise et le suivi quotidien des plateformes de télésurveillance métrologique : deux solutions sont actuellement utilisées, l'une auprès d'un fournisseur couvrant la majorité du parc, l'autre auprès d'un second fournisseur actuellement en phase de test.

    • Superviser l'outil interne propriétaire de l'entreprise, connecté aux équipements et générant des alertes en temps réel en cas de dérive de température.

    • Remonter au service IT les besoins d'évolution et contribuer au développement et à l'amélioration continue de ces outils.

     

    Coordination avec le parc automobile et l'exploitation

    • Travailler avec le Responsable Parc pour planifier les installations, maintenances et immobilisations des véhicules.

    • Coordonner avec l'Exploitation afin de limiter l'impact des interventions sur l'activité.

    • Veiller à la disponibilité opérationnelle des véhicules conformes aux exigences de température.

    • Assurer la sensibilisation et la formation des conducteurs aux bonnes pratiques de maintien de la chaîne du froid (chargement, fermeture, temps d'ouverture des portes, contrôles visuels).

    • Tenir à jour un tableau de bord des non-conformités température et en assurer le suivi avec la facturation des pénalités associées.

    • Assurer le reporting Qualité de Service auprès des Responsables Exploitation et du Commerce, afin d'assurer le suivi avec le client et de le rassurer sur les actions menées.

     

    Gestion des fournisseurs

    • Identifier et sélectionner les fournisseurs de matériels et de prestations métrologiques.

    • Participer aux consultations, appels d'offres et négociations.

    • Suivre les contrats de maintenance et les performances des prestataires.

    • Assurer une veille technologique sur les équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

     

    Qualité et amélioration continue

    • Participer aux audits internes et externes.

    • Élaborer les procédures et instructions de travail.

    • Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance.

    • Conduire les analyses de causes en cas de non-conformité.

    • Proposer des actions d'amélioration continue.

    • Représenter la métrologie lors des audits qualité menés directement par les clients laboratoires et préparer les éléments de preuve associés (certificats d'étalonnage, historiques de température).

     

    ACTIVITES DECISIONNELLES

    Le Responsable Métrologie est amené à :

    • proposer les investissements en matériels de mesure et équipements frigorifiques ;

    • valider les choix techniques des installations ;

    • décider des actions à engager en cas de dérive de température ou de non-conformité ;

    • arbitrer les solutions techniques en lien avec les contraintes opérationnelles ;

    • sélectionner les fournisseurs dans le cadre de sa délégation.

    • Toutes ces décisions devront être validées avec la Direction des Opérations.

     

    RELATIONS FONCTIONNELLES

    En interne

    • Direction des Opérations

    • Responsable Parc Automobile

    • Responsable Exploitation

    • Service Qualité

    • Conducteurs

    • Commerce (reporting Qualité de Service et suivi client lié aux non-conformités température).

    En externe

    • Fournisseurs d'équipements frigorifiques

    • Prestataires de métrologie

    • Clients laboratoires, dans le cadre des audits qualité et des demandes de justificatifs métrologiques.

     


    PROFIL RECHERCHE

    Formation

    At Vio we believe booking accommodation should feel smart, fair, and effortless — never overwhelming or unclear.

    As one of the world’s fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of users make smarter travel decisions by comparing stays across 100+ booking sites — so they can find the perfect place, at the best price, anywhere in the world. We cut through the noise and complexity of hotel and vacation rental booking, surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays — booked with confidence. With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology travelers can trust.

    Who we're looking for

    We are looking for a hands-on Quality Platform Lead to own Vio's quality strategy and automation platform across web, mobile, browser extensions, internal tooling and related surfaces.

    This is a technical leadership role (Staff IC) reporting to the Director of Engineering. You define what good looks like for quality, decide where scarce testing effort goes, and give teams the confidence to ship. Your levers are release gates, quality telemetry, and a developer experience that makes the right tests easy to write and keep alive.

    Product engineers own the tests for the features they build. Your remit is the platform, the strategy and the enablement that make that work hold up at scale. There is no QA department here and we have no plans to create one.

    Where you'll start

    • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

    • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

    • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

    • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

    • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

    • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

    The tooling can stay as it is. With a clear case you can migrate or rebuild. E2E coverage today is thin, so a different platform is genuinely on the table if it serves speed, maintainability and DX better. We have no predefined answer.

    AI-assisted tooling is an open area too. We have no established practice for agent-generated tests or AI-assisted triage, so your judgment on what earns a place in the platform carries real weight.

    What we lack today is clear ownership of strategy, release gates and shared quality telemetry, plus a low-friction path for engineers to spend their testing effort on the highest-risk scenarios.

    How the role works

    Your time splits between hands-on platform work, enablement, strategy and stakeholder telemetry. One insourced QA Engineer supports you. You own the technical direction, the standards and the quality outcomes.

    Once the platform has low friction, product engineers write and maintain the tests for the domains they own. You enable that through patterns, docs, reusable modules, CI checks and risk-based guidance. Gatekeeping releases sits outside the role.

    Expect no direct people-management responsibilities in the near future. Any further QE hire gets evaluated against the ~1:50 rule once the value is proven, and we have no committed headcount plan beyond that.

    What you'll own

    Quality strategy and platform

    • Own the quality strategy and the automation platform across products, covering direction, standards and day-to-day health

    • Decide whether to keep, evolve or replace the current tooling, with clear trade-offs on speed, maintainability and DX

    • Set coding standards and patterns for test code, and keep the suite focused on the tests that earn their place

    Release gates and telemetry

    • Build automated release gates into CI/CD and define what protects the core journeys

    • Give Product, Engineering and leadership real-time quality telemetry on release readiness, risk and pipeline health

    • Put failure triage and flaky-test quarantine in place, so every failure is worth acting on

    Risk-based coverage and testability

    • Work with Product and Engineering to protect high-impact journeys and APIs

    • Retire flaky and low-value tests, and concentrate effort where the risk is highest

    • Act as the technical stakeholder for testability (hooks, mocks, contract tests, test data) and get those improvements onto team roadmaps

    Developer enablement

    • Make it easy for product engineers to write, run and maintain tests locally and in CI

    • Embed quality into how teams plan and ship, and mentor the insourced QA Engineer

    • Drive a measurable increase in developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX

    What success looks like in 12 months

    1. Platform ownership. You have taken over the automation platform across products and own it outright, with direction, standards and health all unambiguous, whether you kept the tooling or replaced it.

    2. Gates and focus. Release gates on the core journeys are fast and deterministic, and testing effort sits on the highest-risk scenarios.

    3. Dev ownership and satisfaction. Writing and maintaining tests is a routine part of Definition of Done, and developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX has measurably improved.

    4. Telemetry. Eng and Product work from live release-readiness and risk dashboards, failures triage cleanly, and flaky tests go into quarantine.

    5. Less manual drag. Regular releases go out without manual testing, with exploratory testing reserved for major new work.

    Who you are

    • You have a track record of building or overhauling automation platforms (SWE / QE / SDET)

    • You write production-grade code across app, test and infra repos. Language matters less to us than depth, though our stack today leans on TypeScript/JS, Elixir, Go, Python and Dart.

    • You use AI agents effectively in your own engineering workflow and can judge where they belong inside a quality platform, from test generation to failure triage

    • You have cross-platform web and mobile automation judgment, and can weigh unified toolchains against separate ones objectively

    • You have deep CI/CD and test infrastructure experience: GitHub Actions, device clouds, parallelisation, test data

    • You can translate quality risk into telemetry and decisions that Eng, Product and leadership act on

    • You are a hands-on builder who wants to code the platform yourself

    • You design platforms developers adopt, and you prioritise risk-based coverage

    Trade-offs we accept: depth on one platform when the other is learnable, and no travel or booking domain background.

    Why join us now?

    • Full ownership of the quality strategy and the automation platform, with a mandate for enablement

    • We are one of the most innovative and fastest-growing accommodation booking platforms in the world today, having grown our bookings 30x between 2017 and 2025, and catering to the needs of over 100 million unique visitors worldwide each year. We do that by harnessing the power of advanced algorithms and an innovative suite of power features and managed to overcome the corona crisis remarkably fast;

    • The mobile applications (iOS and Android) we launched in 2023 are already a big success, reaching 5 million installs with great customer reviews, as we are beginning to build Vio as the brand for value-seeking travellers worldwide;

    • We enjoy getting together to celebrate our wins with company events in Amsterdam and abroad;

    • A budget for your dream home office;

💸 Compensation

Our pay scale ranges from $40/hr to $120/hr pending seniority (& team leadership experience), and our projects are rarely less than 8 full time weeks at 40 hours per week.

We prefer long standing relationships with highly accountable and communicative team members, so we encourage candidates to expect longer term engagements.

 
🎤 How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

 
👩‍🏭 How we work:

We believe that there’s a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason Sanctuary works differently to most shops:

  • Transparency & Ownership: We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.
  • 150% Carbon Negative: Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. We have been certified climate neutral since 2021.
  • Strong Morals: Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).
  • Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.
  • Remote Friendly: Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.
  • Ideas & Products: In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?

→ Read more on our Substack, over here, or our Medium, over there.

 
Important Reminders

Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.

Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! Thank you! :)

Description

Primary responsibilities for administration and development & integration support for Splunk Cloud. Develops, recommends, implements, and manages the technical architecture (hardware, software, database, and communications) which will be used for all or specific applications in a large, distributed cross-platform environment. Responsibilities also include the identification of relevant information and the determination of the environment, which will be used for development.

In this role the Senior SIEM Architect will:

  • Provide engineering and operational support for the Splunk Cloud Security Incident and Event Management (SIEM) platform. This includes assisting with the implementation and support of SPLUNK Cloud across multiple environments and varying OS types.
  • Provide integration support and development effort on design related changes or introduction of new business requirements to Splunk Cloud.
  • Support ongoing work efforts to develop and administer Splunk Cloud can continue as new requirements, functionality or integration is required to enable our modern enterprise security monitoring program and target state operating model within the current project timelines.

General Skills:

  • Leadership experience in the development and implementation of technical security architectures at the specified experience level
  • Extensive experience with at least two cloud service providers (i.e. AWS, Azure, GCP) , enterprise security services, Identity and database technologies, and network access protocols
  • Experience in structured methodologies for the design, development and implementation of cloud applications
  • Extensive experience in systems analysis and design in large secure solution environments
  • Knowledge and experience designing processes around ITIL and is able to guide others using this methodology
  • Experience translating business requirements into solution needs
  • Experience preparing conceptual, logical and/or physical processes and data models
  • Experience developing, recommending, implementing and managing technical security architecture
  • Awareness of emerging technologies, trends and directions
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills; verbal and written communication skills; interpersonal and negotiation skills
  • A team player with a track record for meeting deadlines
  • Knowledge and understanding of Information Management security principles, concepts, policies and practices

SkillsExperience and Skill Set Requirements

Experience and Skill Set Requirements

Advanced knowledge and experience with Security Information & Event Management technology: (45%)

SIEM:

  • SPLUNK Cloud (Must)
  • Azure Sentinel

Cloud Infrastructure:

  • Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
  • Platform as a Service (PaaS)
  • Software as a Service (SaaS)

Agile Project Delivery (15%)

Experience working on agile project delivery teams. Working experience with:

  • Backlog
  • User stories
  • Scrum
  • Sprints

Security Operations Experience (35%)

  • SIEM use case development, rationalization and configuration.
  • SIEM dashboard creation
  • Security operational process development and documentation (playbooks/runbooks)
  • MITRE Framework

Previous Public Sector Experience (5%)

  • Previous public sector work experience is considered a positive

Must haves:

Advanced knowledge and experience with Security Information & Event Management technology

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States. LendingTree and its affiliates (“LendingTree”) will not provide or assume sponsorship for employment visas for this position, now or in the future.

The Opportunity
As a Data Engineer at LendingTree, you’ll build the pipelines, models, and data services behind reporting, analytics, and data science across our lending and insurance businesses. You’ll tackle complex integration and modeling challenges, improve reliability and cost efficiency, and apply practical AI tools to help the team deliver better data solutions faster.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Build and operate scalable batch and real-time streaming pipelines, ETL/ELT workflows, and database applications across multiple lines of business, with clear plans for schema changes, retries, and recovery.
  • Design dimensional models and reusable datasets for business, analytics, and data science needs. Perform complex data analysis to validate business rules, identify trends and anomalies, and uncover opportunities.
  • Own the reliability and efficiency of your data solutions: automate quality checks, monitor freshness, tune performance and compute costs, and participate in the on-call rotation to resolve incidents and prevent recurrence.
  • Create reusable frameworks and development patterns that improve delivery speed and consistency. Apply automated testing, code review, and repeatable deployments; maintain technical standards, runbooks, and learning materials.
  • Partner with business users and engineering teams to clarify requirements, resolve issues, and contribute to the data engineering roadmap, including platform capabilities, priorities, technical trade-offs, and delivery estimates.
  • Apply AI tools to development, testing, documentation, and troubleshooting. Validate generated code and results, protect sensitive data, and assess whether these tools improve quality and reduce delivery time.

Who You’ll Work With

You’ll join the Data Engineering team, working with your manager, fellow engineers, and partners in analytics, data science, product, and business operations across Lending and Insurance. You’ll also collaborate with platform and infrastructure teams to manage dependencies, support production services, and turn business priorities into practical data solutions.

What You’ll Bring

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in data engineering, including data warehousing, ETL/ELT development, and analytics, with a record of delivering and supporting production solutions.
  • Advanced SQL skills, including writing, tuning, and debugging complex queries and using data analysis to investigate problems.
  • Experience designing data lakes and warehouses on scalable, distributed platforms, with an understanding of batch and streaming integration patterns.
  • Strong dimensional modeling skills and sound data warehousing practices, including defining grain, fact and dimension tables, and how historical changes are represented.
  • Ability to deliver projects with minimal guidance in an Agile team, using testing, version control, documentation, and systematic troubleshooting to build maintainable solutions.
  • Clear written, verbal, and data presentation skills, including the ability to understand business needs and explain findings and technical decisions through documentation, presentations, or dashboards.

What Will Help You Thrive
You’re curious about the business behind the data, learn new tools thoughtfully, communicate issues early, and share both credit and lessons learned. Experience in any of the following is a plus:

  • Snowflake virtual warehouses, performance and cost tuning, Streams and Tasks, and/or SQL Server.
  • Matillion, dbt, or similar tools for data integration and transformation.
  • Python, C#, or PowerShell for integration and automation; Git/GitLab for collaboration and CI/CD workflows.
  • Power BI, Tableau, or Streamlit for dashboards, data applications, and communicating insights.
  • using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Maia to accelerate coding, testing, documentation, and troubleshooting while validating generated code and results.
  • S. in Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

What Success Looks Like

  • Production pipelines meet agreed freshness and reliability targets, with clear monitoring, ownership, and recovery procedures.
  • Business, analytics, and data science partners use tested models with consistent definitions and less manual reconciliation.
  • Query tuning and pipeline improvements produce measurable reductions in runtime, compute cost, or recurring incidents.
  • Reusable frameworks, useful documentation, and validated AI workflows shorten delivery time while maintaining quality.

Life at LendingTree

We’re a collaborative, entrepreneurial team that’s curious, creative, and always ready to roll up our sleeves and get things done. You’ll work alongside smart, driven people who care about doing great work — and about helping each other succeed.

We believe the best ideas come from different perspectives, and we’re committed to creating a workplace where people feel welcomed, valued, and empowered to make an impact. You’ll have the trust and flexibility to do your best work, the opportunity to take ownership and try new things, and teammates who genuinely enjoy working together.

And while we work hard, we don’t take ourselves too seriously. We celebrate wins, recognize great work (our GSD — Get Stuff Done — Award is a fan favorite), and make time to have some fun along the way.

Come grow with us, make an impact, and help us build what’s next.

What We Offer

We want you to feel supported at work and beyond. Our benefits and programs are designed to help you stay healthy, recharge, plan for the future, and bring your best to whatever matters most to you.

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) matching
  • Generous time off
  • Wellness programs and resources
  • Annual performance bonus eligibility

Base Pay:

The base pay range for this position is $100,000-130,000; pay offered may vary based on location, internal factors, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Incentive Compensation: This position is eligible for an annual performance bonus.

Work Authorization: This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. Please do not apply for this role if you will need employer sponsorship now or in the future to begin or continue employment.

Everyone Belongs Here

LendingTree is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion (or creed), gender, gender expression, age, national origin, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or military status.

If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to submit an application, please email us at .

Company: TurFresh

Location: Remote — Pacific Time availability required

Engagement: Project-based contractor, with opportunities for ongoing assignments

About TurFresh

TurFresh specializes in professional artificial turf cleaning and maintenance across multiple U.S. markets. We help homeowners and businesses keep their turf clean, fresh, and ready to enjoy.

We’re looking for a reliable freelance designer who can turn marketing ideas, photography, and raw video footage into polished content that educates customers, builds trust, and supports sales. You’ll work with our marketing team and complement our Social & Reputation role by producing the creative assets they need.

What You’ll Create

    • Social media graphics, educational carousels, and campaign assets.

    • Short-form videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts using footage provided by our team.

    • Digital advertising graphics and video variations for testing different hooks, messages, and calls to action.

    • Email graphics for promotions, customer education, and maintenance reminders.

    • Website and landing page graphics.

    • Before-and-after content, customer testimonials, and service explainers.

    • Sales materials explaining our cleaning process, maintenance plans, and service value.

    • Occasional flyers, brochures, and other print materials.

Required Skills

    • A strong portfolio of marketing design for consumer brands or service businesses.

    • Basic short-form video editing: selecting useful footage, creating engaging openings, trimming clips, adding captions, balancing audio, and formatting for each platform.

    • Strong layout, typography, and visual storytelling skills.

    • Ability to make educational content clear and engaging.

    • Ability to follow brand guidelines while contributing thoughtful creative ideas.

    • Strong English communication, attention to detail, and dependable delivery.

    • Comfort working from briefs, asking useful questions, and incorporating feedback.

    • Proficiency in relevant design and video tools, such as Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, Figma, CapCut, or comparable software.

    • Organized delivery of editable source files and finished assets.

    Experience with home services, pet-related brands, or local service marketing is a plus.

Availability & Working Together

    Consistent availability during Pacific Time business hours is required. We need someone who can collaborate while our team is working, participate in project discussions, and respond to feedback and revision requests during agreed availability windows.

    You can be located anywhere, provided your schedule offers reliable overlap with our team. Please specify your regular available hours in Pacific Time and your current capacity for new projects.

    Our marketing team will provide objectives, key messages, brand assets, photography, and raw footage—including field content captured by our team. You’ll turn those inputs into finished creative and identify anything else needed to complete the assignment.

    Each project will have an agreed scope, deliverables, deadline, fee, and revision allowance. This role focuses on creative production; our team handles marketing strategy, publishing, community engagement, and reputation management.

What Success Looks Like

    • Clear, engaging creative that helps customers understand our services and their value.

    • Effective use of real customer and field footage.

    • Consistent branding across graphics and video.

    • Reliable turnaround, proactive communication, and accurate execution.

    • Assets delivered in the right formats, ready for our team to use.

To Apply

    Please include:

    1. Your portfolio, with three relevant graphic design examples and at least two short-form video examples.

    1. A brief explanation of your contribution to those examples.

    1. Your preferred design and video editing tools.

    1. Your time zone, regular availability in Pacific Time, and weekly capacity for new assignments.

    1. Your typical turnaround for a graphic, a short-form video, and revisions.

    1. Your project pricing or estimated fees for a social carousel, a set of three ad variations, and a 15–30-second video edited from supplied footage.

    1. Your earliest available start date.

    We plan to begin with a small paid project to evaluate creative quality, communication, turnaround, and fit before assigning additional work.

TurFresh shares a Lever recruiting platform with our sister company, Express Chipping. As a result, you may see the Express Chipping name in the application URL or automated communications. This position is exclusively with TurFresh.

We are seeking professionals with expertise in Medicaid policy, program design, or program administration.

We welcome policy analysts, program specialists, researchers, agency professionals, and experienced practitioners. Your expertise may be concentrated in one Medicaid area or span several disciplines.

  • Compare state approaches and identify relevant practices.
  • Support stakeholder interviews, working groups, and public engagement.

  • Collaborate with operational, legal, clinical, and analytical specialists.

  • Strong research, writing, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex program information and explain its practical implications.

Preferred Experience

Aperia is unlocking a new era of efficiency and sustainability for commercial vehicle fleets, by developing innovative hardware and data analytics solutions. Inventors of the award- winning and disruptive Halotm Automatic Tire Inflator, and the cloud delivered Halo Connect tire analytics platform. Aperia saves fleets thousands of hours of down-time every week, reduces the carbon footprint and environmental impact of the freight industry. Join us as we expand our product offering and take the next steps on our journey toward bringing the "backbone of our economy" into the automation age.

This position requires candidates to be authorized to work in the US on an ongoing basis without current or future employer sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor or transfer H-1B or other employment-based visas, and candidates currently on F-1, OPT, STEM OPT status are not eligiable for this role.

Your Role

As a Hardware Data Analyst, you will harness vast amounts of data streaming from our extensive deployment of telematics and IoT devices in the field. Your work will directly impact our hardware systems' performance, reliability, and efficiency, helping deliver exceptional customer experiences. Collaborating with engineering, product management, data science, and customer support teams, you will process and analyze sensor and analytics data to uncover insights, identify issues, and drive continuous improvement.

Your Responsibilities

  • Design and deliver dashboards, reports, and presentations using tools like QuickSight, Tableau, or Python libraries to visualize performance metrics and communicate findings effectively.
  • Continuously monitor and analyze incoming sensor and analytics data to identify trends, anomalies, and potential issues in the field.
  • Use statistical models and machine learning techniques to extract insights and generate actionable recommendations for hardware reliability and performance improvements.
  • Compare outputs from various firmware versions to validate improvements or detect unexpected regressions.
  • Collaborate with hardware engineers, product managers, and data scientists to define and execute data analysis strategies.
  • Support customer support teams by providing data-driven insights to address product performance and anomaly-related inquiries.
  • Proactively identify and propose new tools, methods, or processes to enhance data analysis capabilities and improve operational efficiency.
  • Collaborate with the engineering and data science teams to design and implement data pipelines that ensure reliable ingestion, processing, and storage of large-scale field data.
  • Act as a data advocate within the organization, ensuring teams have the necessary data access and tools to make informed decisions.
  • Collaborate with product development teams to ensure field data is incorporated into the design of future hardware and software features.

Skills/Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • 2-4 years of experience in data analysis, with exposure to hardware-related roles or IoT systems preferred.
  • Proficiency in Python, SQL, MATLAB, or Excel for data analysis and modeling.
  • Demonstrated experience with visualization tools like Quicksight, Tableau, Streamlit, or Looker.
  • Strong understanding of statistical modeling, machine learning, and time-series data analysis.
  • Experience with cloud platforms like AWS (S3, Redshift, Kinesis, IoT Core) or similar is a plus.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to translate data findings into actionable insights.
  • Excellent communication skills to present complex data in a clear, concise manner to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Pay Range: $95,000 - $123,000

*Base salary only. Salary is dependent on multiple factors including, but not limited to, experience and location.

**Additional compensation may include equity, bonuses, stipends, medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and long-term disability insurance.
